policy: Exactly 20 logical programs: 5 Python-only (A), 5 C-only (B), 10 pair halves (C) forming 5 matched pairs. C-05 is ONE logical program across 3 files. Error fixtures are NOT counted. Expected outputs verified with host toolchains (scripts/dev/m7_verify_demos.sh).

demos.title: Fundamentals: variables, expressions, functions, branching

guided.simple: A tiny program computes a triangle area twice and checks the result is valid.
guided.detailed: Watch the recorded trace: `area` is called twice with different arguments, the branch inside it takes the same path both times, and each return value flows back to the module frame.
guided.technical: Bytecode: CALL/RETURN under sys.settrace; locals snapshots show base/height per call. Python 3.12 bytecode is version-pinned; no LLVM IR exists here.

capabilities.memory: AVAILABLE (frame snapshots, id()-based aliases, bounded object graph, tracemalloc/gc)
capabilities.optimization: UNAVAILABLE (Python has no LLVM -O levels; bytecode comparison is version-pinned CPython)

limits: Trace caps: 5000 events / 64 frames / 200 locals (not reached here).

demos.title: Loops and collections: accumulator with filtering

guided.simple: One loop walks a list, sums everything, and collects the even numbers.
guided.detailed: The line-event stream shows FOR_ITERATION jumps: the loop body runs 8 times and the branch appends only 3 values. Locals snapshots show the accumulator grow from call to call.
guided.technical: Bytecode: FOR_ITER/COMPARE_OP/JUMP_ABSOLUTE pattern; list.append is a C builtin (no Python frame, hence no call events for it).

demos.title: True recursion: frame growth and unwinding

guided.simple: fib(12) calls itself 465 times; the trace shows the call stack grow and shrink.
guided.detailed: The replay timeline shows depth increasing to 12 and unwinding; each frame has its own `n` (see locals). The 465 count includes both leaf and inner calls (2*F(13)-1).
guided.technical: Tree recursion: calls(fib)=2*F(13)-1=465. Depth cap is 64 — this program peaks at 12, so the full tree is recorded.

demos.title: Closure, generator suspension, exception scope
demos.expected_stdout:
counter=15,17
pairs=0,4
suspended=yes
caught=scope demo
finally=finally-ran

guided.simple: A closure keeps private state, a generator pauses twice, and an exception is caught with a finally block.
guided.detailed: The generator's frame_id stays STABLE across suspensions (M5QA fix): a yield is a suspension, not a frame death. The manual next() consumes one value (pairs=0,4 — the 2 is skipped), demonstrating the iterator protocol vs the for-loop protocol. The closure's `count` survives between calls.
guided.technical: Generator resumption re-fires 'call' events (CPython semantics); CO_GENERATOR frames are not popped at yield. Exception records name the instance; user __str__ is never evaluated by the tracer.

capabilities.optimization: UNAVAILABLE (Python has no LLVM -O levels; bytecode comparison is version-pinned CPython)

limits: Generator memory previews show identity, not contents of suspended frames.

demos.title: Classes, imports, bounded concurrency

guided.simple: Two threads compute results into preassigned slots; a small class accumulates a total.
guided.detailed: join() makes the outcome deterministic because each thread writes its OWN slot — the output does not depend on scheduling. The recorded trace shows only the main thread (sys.settrace is per-thread) — an honest limitation.
guided.technical: Worker threads are NOT traced (settrace is thread-local); results are index-addressed to avoid order dependence. GIL interleaving is not observed and not claimed.

capabilities.memory: AVAILABLE (frame snapshots, id()-based aliases, bounded object graph, tracemalloc/gc)
capabilities.optimization: UNAVAILABLE (Python has no LLVM -O levels; bytecode comparison is version-pinned CPython)

limits: Thread interleaving is unobservable in the trace — scheduling limitations are declared, not hidden.

demos.title: Expressions, functions, branching → LLVM IR

guided.simple: Two small functions clamp and average values; the IR shows the unoptimized bodies.
guided.detailed: At -O0 the IR loads/stores every local through the stack; OptimizationLab shows -O2 collapsing the arithmetic. The recorded trace shows call/return for clamp and weighted.
guided.technical: Instrumented with -finstrument-functions (call/return events, no ptrace); clamp is inlined at -O2 (verify in OptimizationLab: the symbol disappears from the O2 build).

capabilities.memory: PARTIAL (C heap via allocator interposition; frame locals unavailable outside the curated gdb profile)
capabilities.optimization: AVAILABLE (OptimizationLab -O0/-O1/-O2)

limits: Static assembly is not an executed-instruction count.

demos.title: Preprocessor, conditional build, loop → CFG

guided.simple: Macros and #if select the build path at COMPILE time; the loop's CFG has a header, body and exit block.
guided.detailed: The preprocess stage shows SCALE(i) expanded to ((i) * 2); DEMO_MODE=2 makes the #else branch dead at compile time — the #else code is never compiled, which the IR/ASM absence shows.
guided.technical: CFG: for-header → if → two successors → latch → exit. Basic-block inventory comes from real clang IR/ASM, not a generic diagram.

limits: #if pruning is a compile-time effect — the trace cannot show it at runtime.

demos.title: Pointers and arrays on the stack

guided.simple: swap() exchanges two array ends through pointers; a bounded slice sum walks the array.
guided.detailed: The IR shows pointer dereferences as loads/stores; swap's effects are visible in the output (first/last exchanged). Pointer arithmetic stays in bounds — the demo never walks past the array.
guided.technical: Array decay: sum_slice receives int* — same machine representation as &arr[0]. Address instability (ASLR) applies to any recorded addresses.

capabilities.optimization: AVAILABLE (OptimizationLab -O0/-O1/-O2)

limits: Out-of-bounds arithmetic would be UB — this demo stays in bounds by design.

demos.title: Structs and dynamic memory (malloc/free, correct path)

guided.simple: Three struct records are allocated on the heap, filled, summed and freed — correctly.
guided.detailed: The allocator interposition records the malloc(3*sizeof(record_t)) with its real size and the matching free: outstanding returns to zero. NULL is checked before use (no UB on OOM).
guided.technical: sizeof(record_t) includes tail padding for the char[8] tag — check the interposed size (3*24) rather than assuming field sums.

limits: Sanitizer availability varies; correct-path malloc/free here means NO diagnostics are expected — absence of findings is not proof of coverage.

demos.title: Multi-file C project: header + 2 translation units

guided.simple: One program in three files: a header declares, one TU implements, the main TU uses it. The LINKER connects them.
guided.detailed: Both TUs are compiled separately (two compile steps in the build record), then linked. The linked binary's symbol table contains math_sum_series and math_gcd defined (T) — that is the cross-TU resolution evidence.
guided.technical: Analysis covers the primary TU's stages; the LINK step evidence (symbols of the final binary) is what proves cross-TU linkage — static analysis of one TU never assumes the other executes independently.

capabilities.analysis: AVAILABLE for the primary TU (main.c); the second TU is compiled and linked, not independently analyzed
capabilities.trace: AVAILABLE (both TUs instrumented; call/return across TUs recorded)
capabilities.memory: PARTIAL (allocator interposition)
capabilities.optimization: AVAILABLE (OptimizationLab builds the primary file; multi-file O-level builds are not wired)

limits: Multi-file linking is a curated-demo capability; pasted multi-file C still runs single-file only.
